target: myers_step: shorter loop-carried critical path on Apple Silicon (aarch64::apple)
hypothesis: Shift before the add (S = (E & P) + P with E = eq << 1, P = vp << 1) and write each output as a two-op select on S: chain 6 -> 5 at 18 ops (was 15), up to ~1/6 less time per column on patterns <= 64 chars.

benchmark_by_length (A1 B1 A2 B2, B/A of.len 16: ascii 1.050/1.042, latin1 1.035/1.029, cjk 1.035/1.030, emoji 1.044/1.033 (IQRs separate: loss)
benchmark_by_length (A1 B1 A2 B2, B/A of.len 32-512: within noise on all kinds (rapidfuzz drift 0.95-1.03)

reason: Wins only one microbenchmark (ASCII long text, ~-4.5%) and loses 3-5% at length 16. About 1.97 ns (~7 cycles at 3.5 GHz) per column with a 6-op chain means the column loop is not limited by the step chain alone; profile what else bounds it before shortening the chain further.

analysis.profile (samply, ascii/cjk 32|64 x 4000): 99% self time in one inlined distance function. ASCII: 19 instructions per column (15 myers_step, 2 eq loads, 2 loop control), 98.5% of samples on the chain-end bic/orr/subs, eq loads ~0%. CJK: 22-25+ instructions per column (hash lookup + probe), myers block 51-57% of samples, the extra lookup work hides behind the same floor (2.13-2.20 ns/col vs 2.17 ASCII).
analysis.latency probe (experiments/latprobe, M2: and/orr/eor/bic/orn/eon/lsl #1/add: 1 cycle each; shifted-operand forms (orr x, y, x lsl #1): 2 cycles. The 6-op critical path alone: 6.0; plus 9 invariant ops: 6.2-6.3; plus 9 ops reading chain values: 6.6-6.9. Isolated blocks (corrected 2026-11-24; the first probe called the block through a function pointer and passed vp/vn through the stack, which reported 7.50/7.19 and 7.65/7.47): chain6 6.68 const eq / 6.51 table eq, chain5 6.61 / 6.24 at 3.35 GHz. The table-eq ratio 0.96 matches the end-to-end ASCII long-text ratio (~0.955).
analysis.conclusion: Both blocks run above their chain length: chain6 by ~0.5 cycles, chain5 by ~1.25. Off-chain ops that read chain values delay the critical ops, and chain5's 3 extra ops and wider fan-out cost most of the cycle it saves. Headroom: ~0.5 cycle (~8%) by reordering chain6; up to ~1.25 cycles (~20%) for a chain-5 form with less interference. Next search: fitness = latprobe table-eq cycles per column.

target: myers_step: fewer cycles per column on Apple Silicon (aarch64::apple), scored by the latprobe table-eq column
hypothesis: chain5's 18 ops in order of readiness (ops with slack last in their cycle), vn' = (xv & N) | (G & !S) so cycle 4 has 2 ops instead of 3, and E | N = xv << 1: chain 5, fewer ops ready with the critical ones; about 0.5 cycles per column below chain6 on the probe.

probe.search: 13 blocks in experiments/latprobe/src/blocks.rs. Program order is the largest lever: random valid orders of chain6 scored 6.73-7.24, of chain5 6.49-6.80; level order is best. Ops that read only eq are cheaper than ops that read vp/vn. 19- and 20-op forms and shifted-operand forms (about 3 per cycle vs about 4.5 for register-register logic ops) were slower.

bench.B: chain5_ge everywhere (benchmark_by_le: lengths 48-64: 0.92-0.97; 72+: neutral; lengths 8-16: 1.02-1.06, worst on CJK/emoji (interleaved 6 pairs: cjk-8/16 and emoji-8/16 1.026-1.043, tight)
bench.D: kept form (chain5_ge except tiny_swar: lengths 48-64: 0.95-0.97 on all kinds (IQRs separate on most cells); 8-32 and 72-512: within noise (0.97-1.02); rapidfuzz drift 0.98-1.02. Emoji length 4: 1.025/1.027, but it runs tiny_n with chain6 in both builds, so it is not the step.
bench.diff test: 400k random pairs (all kinds, mixed kinds, lengths 0-3000) match rapidfuzz
bench.CI A/B macos-arm64 (macos-15 runner, App: single-word cases: ascii-24-vs-384 0.896, ascii-24-vs-96 0.939, ascii-32-dis 0.945, ascii-48-d6 0.946, latin1-32-dis 0.955, latin1-64-dis 0.934, ucs2-32 0.968, ucs4-64 0.967, ascii-12-dis 1.028; geomean over 90 cases 0.995

reason: Wins 3-5% at lengths 48-64 on every kind and 7-10% on short patterns against long texts (ASCII, CJK 64, ASCII 9-16), no loss beyond noise elsewhere. chain5_ge alone lost 3-7% in tiny_n and tiny_swar: there the match mask takes integer ops, and the 3 extra ops compete with them. Where the mask is loaded (peq table, hash) or computed on the vector units (NEON), the shorter chain wins. So the dispatcher selects per loop: kernels::myers_step_few_ops (chain6) for tiny_swar and tiny_n, kernels::myers_step (chain5_ge) elsewhere.
lesson: The probe's table-eq column predicts loops whose mask is a load; it does not see loops that spend integer ops on the mask. Score candidates for those with a column that computes eq with integer ops, or keep the fewest-ops form there.

target: myers_step: the chain-5 algebra of myers_step-apple-chain5-ge on Neoverse (aarch64::neoverse)
hypothesis: Neoverse runs logical ops with a shifted operand in one cycle, so the four lsl of the Apple form fold into their consumers: chain 6 -> 5 at the same op count (LLVM emits 14 ALU ops per column for both forms), up to ~1/6 less time on chain-bound loops.

hardware: GitHub ubuntu-24.04 (CPU model not logged) and windows-2025 (AMD Family 26 = Zen 5) runners
target: myers_step: the chain-5 algebra on x86-64 (x86_64::bmi1::myers_step_andn)
hypothesis: With vp' = !A ^ (!D | S) and the and-nots as BMI1 andn, the chain drops from 6 to 5 at 18 ALU ops (15 before); a gain where the core has enough ALUs to absorb 3 more ops.
codegen: Without barriers LLVM forms S with a scaled lea and factors xv out of vn' (xv & (N | !(E|P|S))), which puts vn' back at chain 6; two values pass through opaque in the candidate. The loop has 18 ALU ops plus 5 register copies (15 + 3 before).

bench.noise floor: CI A/B run 45479455375 (Apple-only change, so these platforms ran identical code): every case within 0.987-1.025
bench.CI A/B windows-x86-64, Zen 5 (run 454825: ascii-24-vs-384 0.886, ascii-24-vs-96 0.931, ascii-48-d6 0.919, latin1-64-dis 0.918, 32-byte cases 0.960-0.972; but ratio:short-ucs4-64 1.070 and affix-ucs4-800 1.065 (untouched paths)
bench.CI A/B linux-x86-64 (run 45482548366, B/: ascii-24-vs-384 1.129, ascii-48-d6 1.060, ucs4-64 1.049, latin1-32-dis 1.034, ascii-24-vs-96 0.955; 13 cases above 1.02, several on untouched paths (medium-ascii-120-sim2 1.084)

reason: Wins ~11% on a 6-ALU core (Zen 5), loses up to 13% on the Linux runner, and shifts untouched cases by 3-8% on both. A core with 4 ALUs, or without move elimination (Ice Lake), cannot absorb 3 more ops plus the copies that two-operand x86 forms need. Revisit with a form that needs fewer ops or copies, or with per-CPU selection.
